items.readable_text:
Content:
Whenever we have a fraction in an equation, we apply the multiplication principle to get rid of it. For example, consider the equation below:
[MATH: \dfrac{2x+12}{3} =6]

Content:
Since the opposite of dividing by [MATH: 3] is multiplying by [MATH: 3], we apply the multiplication principle and multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: 3]:

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
\eqalign{
\dfrac{2x+12}{3} &=6\
3 \cdot \left(\dfrac{2x+12}{3}\right) &= 3 \cdot 6\
\cancel{3} \cdot \left(\dfrac{2x+12}{\cancel{3}}\right) &= 18 \
2x+12 &= 18
}]

Content:
The process of removing the fraction is called clearing the rational expression. We now have an equation that we can solve using the usual methods:
[MATH: \eqalign{
2x+12 &= 18\
2x+12-12 &=18-12 \
2x &=6 \
\dfrac{2x}{2} &=\dfrac{6}{2} \
x &=3
}]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by [MATH: 2\mathbin{:}] [MATH: \eqalign{ 13 &= \dfrac{6y+8}{2} \ 2 \cdot 13 &= 2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{2}\right) \ 2 \cdot 13 &= \cancel{2} \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{\cancel{2}}\right) \ 26 &= 6y+8 }]

Next, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

[MATH: \eqalign{ 26 &= 6y+8 \ 26-8 &= 6y+8-8 \ 18 &= 6y \ \dfrac{18}{6} &= \dfrac{6y}{6} \ 3 &= y }]

Thus, [MATH: y=3.]

First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by [MATH: 3.] We must make sure that all of the terms on the right-hand side are multiplied by [MATH: 3.]

[MATH: (2n + 6)/(3)|= 4n + 1; 3 ⋅ ((2n + 6)/(3))|= 3 ⋅ (4n + 1); 3 ⋅ ((2n + 6)/(3))|= 3 ⋅ 4n + 3 ⋅ 1; 2n + 6|= 12n + 3]

Next, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

[MATH: 2n + 6|= 12n + 3; 2n + 6 − 2n|= 12n + 3 − 2n; 6|= 10n + 3; 6 − 3|= 10n + 3 − 3; 3|= 10n; (3)/(10)|= (10n)/(10); (3)/(10)|= n]

Thus, [MATH: n = \dfrac{3}{10}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Whenever we have a fraction in an equation, we apply the multiplication principle to get rid of it. For example, consider the equation below:
[MATH: \dfrac{2x+12}{3} =6]

Content:
Since the opposite of dividing by [MATH: 3] is multiplying by [MATH: 3], we apply the multiplication principle and multiply both sides of the equation by [MATH: 3]:

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
\eqalign{
\dfrac{2x+12}{3} &=6\
3 \cdot \left(\dfrac{2x+12}{3}\right) &= 3 \cdot 6\
\cancel{3} \cdot \left(\dfrac{2x+12}{\cancel{3}}\right) &= 18 \
2x+12 &= 18
}]

Content:
The process of removing the fraction is called clearing the rational expression. We now have an equation that we can solve using the usual methods:
[MATH: \eqalign{
2x+12 &= 18\
2x+12-12 &=18-12 \
2x &=6 \
\dfrac{2x}{2} &=\dfrac{6}{2} \
x &=3
}]

---

Item 2 — Example: Clearing a Rational Expression With a Variable on One Side

Example Prompt:
Solve the equation [MATH: 13 = \dfrac{6y+8}{2}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by [MATH: 2\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: \eqalign{
13 &= \dfrac{6y+8}{2} \
2 \cdot 13 &= 2 \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{2}\right) \
2 \cdot 13 &= \cancel{2} \cdot \left(\dfrac{6y+8}{\cancel{2}}\right) \
26 &= 6y+8
}]

Next, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

[MATH: \eqalign{
26 &= 6y+8 \
26-8 &= 6y+8-8 \
18 &= 6y \
\dfrac{18}{6} &= \dfrac{6y}{6} \
3 &= y
}]

Thus, [MATH: y=3.]
